blocks.instruction: Complete the sentences below. Choose NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER from the passage for each answer.

people.name: Bongani Ashworth
people.role: volunteer guide who has led tours at the museum for eleven years

people.name: Imogen Szczepanski
people.role: head of learning at the museum

paragraphs.text: Entry to the museum's permanent galleries is free for everyone, although we welcome donations at the boxes beside the main entrance. Our special exhibitions, which change three times a year, do require a ticket. These can be bought online up to a month in advance, and booking ahead is strongly recommended: each ticket is for a timed entry slot, and weekend slots frequently sell out by Friday afternoon. A limited number of tickets are kept back for sale at the front desk each morning. Reduced prices apply to students, people over 65 and those receiving unemployment benefits, while under-fives go free. If you expect to come more than twice in a year, an annual pass usually works out cheaper and lets you skip the queue. The museum is open from 10 a.m. to 5.30 p.m. every day except 24–26 December, with a late opening until 9 p.m. on Fridays.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Our volunteer guides lead a free highlights tour twice a day, at 11 a.m. and 2 p.m., starting from the large whale skeleton in the entrance hall. The tour lasts about 45 minutes and covers six of the museum's best-known objects, making it ideal for first-time visitors. There is no need to book, but places are limited to twenty people per tour and are given out on a first-come, first-served basis. Groups of ten or more who would like their own private tour should contact us at least three weeks before their visit. 'People often tell us the tour changed the way they saw the rest of the building,' says Bongani Ashworth, who has guided visitors here for eleven years. If you prefer to explore at your own pace, audio guides in nine languages can be hired from the information desk; a small deposit is charged and returned when the device is handed back. A tour in British Sign Language runs on the first Saturday of every month.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Large bags, suitcases and umbrellas are not permitted in the galleries and must be left in the cloakroom on the lower ground floor, where lockers take a one-pound coin that is returned when you collect your belongings. All floors can be reached by lift, and wheelchairs can be borrowed free of charge from the information desk, though they cannot be reserved in advance. Baby-changing facilities are available on every floor. The ground-floor café serves hot and cold food throughout the day, while the rooftop restaurant takes bookings only. Visitors who have brought their own lunch are welcome to use the picnic room next to the cloakroom. For anyone who finds the galleries overwhelming, a quiet room with soft lighting is located on the second floor and is open to all visitors.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Children are at the heart of what we do. Families can collect an explorer backpack, containing a magnifying glass, sketching materials and a trail leading to ten hidden animals around the building, from the Family Desk. Backpacks are free, but we ask for a form of photo identification, which we keep until the backpack is returned. 'We designed the trails so that adults learn as much as the children,' explains Imogen Szczepanski, head of learning. 'Parents tell us they notice things they'd walked past for years.' Every Saturday and Sunday, drop-in craft workshops run in the Discovery Studio between 11 a.m. and 3 p.m.; no booking is needed. Our monthly sleepovers allow children aged seven to eleven to spend the night among the dinosaurs. At least one adult must stay with every group of up to five children, and these events usually fill up within days of being announced.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: The museum is a five-minute walk from Riverside underground station. On-site parking is very limited and reserved for visitors with disabilities, so we encourage everyone else to come by public transport or bicycle; racks can be found by the east gate. Photography for personal use is allowed in the permanent galleries, provided you switch off your flash, but cameras are not allowed in special exhibitions because many objects are on loan from other collections. The museum shop, beside the main exit, stocks books, toys and gifts, and every purchase helps fund our work. Comments can be left at the information desk or on our website.
paragraphs.label: E

section.text:
Your Visit to the National Museum

A. Entry to the museum's permanent galleries is free for everyone, although we welcome donations at the boxes beside the main entrance. Our special exhibitions, which change three times a year, do require a ticket. These can be bought online up to a month in advance, and booking ahead is strongly recommended: each ticket is for a timed entry slot, and weekend slots frequently sell out by Friday afternoon. A limited number of tickets are kept back for sale at the front desk each morning. Reduced prices apply to students, people over 65 and those receiving unemployment benefits, while under-fives go free. If you expect to come more than twice in a year, an annual pass usually works out cheaper and lets you skip the queue. The museum is open from 10 a.m. to 5.30 p.m. every day except 24–26 December, with a late opening until 9 p.m. on Fridays.

B. Our volunteer guides lead a free highlights tour twice a day, at 11 a.m. and 2 p.m., starting from the large whale skeleton in the entrance hall. The tour lasts about 45 minutes and covers six of the museum's best-known objects, making it ideal for first-time visitors. There is no need to book, but places are limited to twenty people per tour and are given out on a first-come, first-served basis. Groups of ten or more who would like their own private tour should contact us at least three weeks before their visit. 'People often tell us the tour changed the way they saw the rest of the building,' says Bongani Ashworth, who has guided visitors here for eleven years. If you prefer to explore at your own pace, audio guides in nine languages can be hired from the information desk; a small deposit is charged and returned when the device is handed back. A tour in British Sign Language runs on the first Saturday of every month.

C. Large bags, suitcases and umbrellas are not permitted in the galleries and must be left in the cloakroom on the lower ground floor, where lockers take a one-pound coin that is returned when you collect your belongings. All floors can be reached by lift, and wheelchairs can be borrowed free of charge from the information desk, though they cannot be reserved in advance. Baby-changing facilities are available on every floor. The ground-floor café serves hot and cold food throughout the day, while the rooftop restaurant takes bookings only. Visitors who have brought their own lunch are welcome to use the picnic room next to the cloakroom. For anyone who finds the galleries overwhelming, a quiet room with soft lighting is located on the second floor and is open to all visitors.

D. Children are at the heart of what we do. Families can collect an explorer backpack, containing a magnifying glass, sketching materials and a trail leading to ten hidden animals around the building, from the Family Desk. Backpacks are free, but we ask for a form of photo identification, which we keep until the backpack is returned. 'We designed the trails so that adults learn as much as the children,' explains Imogen Szczepanski, head of learning. 'Parents tell us they notice things they'd walked past for years.' Every Saturday and Sunday, drop-in craft workshops run in the Discovery Studio between 11 a.m. and 3 p.m.; no booking is needed. Our monthly sleepovers allow children aged seven to eleven to spend the night among the dinosaurs. At least one adult must stay with every group of up to five children, and these events usually fill up within days of being announced.

E. The museum is a five-minute walk from Riverside underground station. On-site parking is very limited and reserved for visitors with disabilities, so we encourage everyone else to come by public transport or bicycle; racks can be found by the east gate. Photography for personal use is allowed in the permanent galleries, provided you switch off your flash, but cameras are not allowed in special exhibitions because many objects are on loan from other collections. The museum shop, beside the main exit, stocks books, toys and gifts, and every purchase helps fund our work. Comments can be left at the information desk or on our website.

questions.prompt: As well as a magnifying glass and a trail, each explorer backpack contains ______.
questions.evidence: a magnifying glass, sketching materials and a trail

explanation.en: Section D lists the contents of the backpack: a magnifying glass, sketching materials and a trail to ten hidden animals.
explanation.ru: В разделе D перечислено, что лежит в рюкзаке: лупа ("magnifying glass"), принадлежности для рисования ("sketching materials") и маршрут поиска десяти спрятанных животных ("trail").
explanation.uk: У розділі D перелічено, що є в рюкзаку: лупа ("magnifying glass"), приладдя для малювання ("sketching materials") і маршрут пошуку десяти схованих тварин ("trail").
